summary: Margaretsville's square wooden lighthouse of 1859 on the Bay of Fundy, one of the first on that shore; kept by the Early family and others, now Coast Guard-owned and society-leased.

lens.note: Fourth-order lens with a single lamp (Lighthouse Friends)

access.note: Coast Guard-owned, leased to the Friends of Margaretsville Lighthouse Society. Grounds open; tower open in summer (Lighthouse Friends). The Lighthouse Directory says the tower is closed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Friends of the Margaretsville Lighthouse Society (leaseholder)

events.note: Residents petition for a light to mark the local pier
Superintendent William Condon drops the plan for a pier beacon after his visit
Square wooden tower built on land donated by Sir Brenton Halliburton
Light moved from a side window to a twelve-sided iron lantern on top of the tower
John Early takes over from his father
Ruth Early (register: Ruth Earley) keeps the light after her husband's death
Fourth-order lens with a single lamp replaces the lamps and reflectors
Fixed red changed to occulting white (Lighthouse Friends)
Electricity replaces the oil lamp; light automated
Friends of the Margaretsville Lighthouse Society formed to seek ownership
Society obtains a lease: Lighthouse Friends says from Fisheries and Oceans; the Directory says from the Coast Guard
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse, register entry 23515, 21 March 2022; announced 2 June 2022

corrections.why: The Coast Guard List of Lights gives 45 03 00.3 N, 065 03 57.8 W, and Lighthouse Friends gives the same point. The record's OSM point is about 100 m away. The register's coordinates (45.04941 N, 65.06492 W) sit between the two. A human should choose the point.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the keeper Ruth Earley, 1907 to 1910, and calls her one of the first women keepers in Nova Scotia. Lighthouse Friends calls her Ruth Early, 1907 to 1909 in its list, while its text says three years. Both are reported in the story; the spelling is not settled.
Lighthouse Friends says the tower is open in summer. The Lighthouse Directory says the site is open and the tower closed. The story reports both and does not promise access.

The Coast Guard list (11.2 m focal height, 9.7 m tower) agrees with the register (9.7 m tower) and with the record. The Lighthouse Directory gives a 9 m focal plane and a 7 m tower; the story does not use those figures.
Lighthouse Friends says the 2018 lease was from the Department of Fisheries and Oceans; the Directory says from the Coast Guard. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Sources: the register (via Heritage Guide), Lighthouse Friends, the Coast Guard List of Lights (Bay of Fundy), the 2022 Parks Canada news release, the Lighthouse Directory and one Marine report page. The core facts agree across the register, the Coast Guard list and Lighthouse Friends: built 1859, 9.7 m tower, Oc(2) W 20s, 11.2 m focal height, 10 nautical miles. Disagreements are reported in the story: Ruth Early or Earley and her end date; access to the tower; the lease holder; the Directory's focal height and tower height. Keeper names from 1911 onward come from Lighthouse Friends. Wesley W. Gaucher is also on the Marine list for the year ended 31 March 1911 (scan page 244, printed p. 237), checked on the page image: the Margaretsville row gives Capt. W. W. Gaucher, appointed March 12, 1909. The Marine tables also list a D. H. McLean at Margaretsville with appointment dates and small remuneration. That looks like a wharf or harbour post, not a light-keeper, so it is not used. Lehan H. Celeveland is spelled as Lighthouse Friends prints it; it may be a misprint for Cleveland, and no source read confirmed the spelling. Storms, wrecks and rescues: no event at this station was found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. The Nova Scotia Lighthouse Preservation Society's interpretive panel PDF returned no text, so it is not used. Lighthouse Friends gives 'Friends of the Margaretsville Lighthouse Society' as the leaseholder and the Coast Guard as owner, which matches the record. The Lighthouse Directory gives the 2018 lease from the Coast Guard, while Lighthouse Friends says DFO; the story gives both. The register date (21 March 2022) and the federal announcement date (2 June 2022) are both used. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Annapolis County is the county in the station brief; none of the footnoted sources names it, and the Directory lists Margaretsville under an Upper Bay of Fundy heading without a county, so the county needs a source before publication. The Directory's focal plane (9 m) and tower (7 m) disagree with the Coast Guard's (11.2 m and 9.7 m); the story now says so.
